Space launch, tracking and control site
The six officers from the National Service Station travel aboard this fleet to the other five regions; actual travel expenses are calculated and deducted at each departure.
Every 10 seconds, each assembler consumes 6 electricity, 1 steel, 0.5 precision parts and 0.3 electronic parts, producing 0.1 spacecraft components.
Every 10 seconds, each technician consumes 4 electricity, 0.5 chemicals, 0.2 medicine, 0.3 glass and 0.2 precision parts, producing 0.1 life support components.

Four registered residents handle tracking and control full-time. System tests and launch prerequisites require an extra 12 electricity to be reserved for ground operations; disabling some assembly workshops can free up allocated power.

All-weather shipping routes and land-sea transfer procedures have been finalized. Neighborhood workshops are authorized to build and repair ocean-going support fleets, opening key transport routes across the deep seas and wastelands.

Territory-wide standards have been established for pollution-resistant water purification technology and mapping mutated ecosystems. The prerequisites for contact with the equatorial rain belt and the inland gravel desert are in place, but fleets, personnel and material aid are still needed.
